label: Euthyphro dependence frame: constitutive dependence among God, nature, approval and goodness
term: constitutive dependence for what a thing is (Euthyphro dependence frame)
definition: A DependenceFrame names God, God's nature, God's act of approving and the standard of goodness, with one primitive relation DependsFor x y: x is what it is because of y (constitutive, explanatory dependence of content). The horns have a literal reading (ApprovedBecauseGood, GoodBecauseApproved) and a consequence reading (IndependentStandard: goodness distinct from God and not depending on him; ConstitutedByApproval: goodness depending on God's approving or being it), disambiguated as EUTHYPHRO_HORN_1 and EUTHYPHRO_HORN_2 (5ceda5e1). NatureProfiles vary which nature God has; PropertyFrame separates the goodness by which God is good from the universal good things share.
note: Analyst formulation; attribution deferred (Plato's Euthyphro, ST I q.3 and q.6 a.3 are unread leads). Example of DependsFor: a club rule depends for its content on the members' vote; the vote's having occurred does not depend on the rule. Distinct from dependence for being on an agent cause (DEPENDENCE_FOR_BEING_VERSUS_STRICT_GROUND_1, which concerns existence) and from Fine's strict ground between facts (sense 2); no inclusion or identity with either is assumed. No structural property is built in: asymmetry is an explicit premise. Its application to God and goodness is an open interpretation, not a claim that the relation is realized.
